reason: First quote and its context state you cannot change AWS managed policy permissions, AWS updates them (most likely when a new service launches) and the update affects all attached principals; second quote states IAM stores up to five versions of customer managed policies for revert.
Quote states AWS managed policies might not grant least privilege because all customers can use them; context recommends reducing permissions further with customer managed policies.
Quote gives the developers-create-roles example and says to use permissions boundaries to set the maximum permissions you delegate.
Quote under the conditions heading gives both examples: require all requests over TLS, and allow actions only when used through a specific service such as CloudFormation.
Quote says to use an IAM role to manage temporary credentials for applications on EC2 so long-term credentials such as access keys are not distributed to the instance.
Best-practices quote requires temporary credentials for human users via an identity provider and assumed roles, and recommends IAM Identity Center for centralized access management; FAQ quote agrees.
Quote states IAM last accessed information helps identify users, roles, permissions, policies and credentials no longer needed so you can remove them.
Quote defines least-privilege permissions as granting only required permissions by defining actions on specific resources under specific conditions.
Context recommends roles with temporary credentials for human users and workloads; quote says where an IAM user or root user is needed, require MFA.
Quote recommends updating access keys when needed, such as when an employee leaves; next sentence in context recommends access last used information to update and remove keys safely.
Quotes state workloads outside AWS (on-premises, other clouds, CI/CD) can use temporary credentials that you must deliver, for example with IAM Roles Anywhere and an X.509 certificate from your PKI.

Quotes state the boundary is set with an AWS managed or customer managed policy for a user or role, is available for service roles but not service-linked roles, and cannot be applied to a service-linked role.

Quotes state a boundary limits but does not provide permissions on its own, effective permissions are the intersection of identity-based policies and the boundary, and an explicit deny in either overrides the allow.

Quotes state grants to a role ARN are limited by an implicit deny in a boundary or session policy, while same-account grants to a role session ARN go directly to the session and are not limited by such implicit denies.

Quote states same-account resource-based grants to an IAM user ARN (not an STS federated user session) are not limited by an implicit deny in an identity-based policy or permissions boundary; the condition is kept.

The 200 percent figure is attributed to Organizations, Control Tower and CloudFormation, but the context attributes the 2 hours instead of 2 weeks account set-up to custom automation on AWS Lambda and Control Tower; the claim's opening clause credits the wrong services for the second value.

Quotes state, with service control policies, developers operate independently with minimal supervision, and IAM Identity Center manages workforce access across more than 350 accounts and 450 applications.
Quotes state the move from per-account manual user creation to IAM Identity Center for the whole organization, and the 10,000-user scan dropping from 25-30 minutes to 1-2 minutes.

Quotes state least privilege by limiting developer access on a list of attributes, granular control with IAM Identity Center permission sets, and just-in-time provisioning for temporary access as the next step.

Two document history rows dated November 26, 2023 add unused access analyzers and custom policy checks; the guide quote lists unused roles, access keys and passwords as findings.

History row dated November 14, 2024 adds centralized root access to remove member-account root credentials; second quote says the management account or IAM delegated administrator does privileged tasks through short-term sessions.

Quotes state an open source MCP server and CLI that analyzes code locally to create baseline identity-based policies for application roles, available at no additional cost.
History row dated January 30, 2025 describes enhanced policy evaluation documentation with improved flow charts and clearer allow or deny explanations.

Organizations history row dated January 23, 2026 states additional services supported by RCPs were added.
